hook: SCP-343 is the Foundation's file on a friendly old man who says he made the universe and can more or less prove it. It is short, warm, and a little sly. Read the addenda with care, since the interesting part happens in what goes missing.
whyItMatters: It is a compact take on a question the site keeps returning to: what containment means when the subject is, by its own account, God. Rather than a threat, it offers an all-powerful being who mostly wants company, which turns the procedures into a polite fiction. Its alleged-god tag places it among other claimed deities, and this one stands out for how little it asks of anyone.
thingsToNotice:
The procedures all but admit defeat: the Foundation cannot hold him, so it keeps him supplied and visited, and his room is bigger inside than out. The effects on staff, from better moods to better health and fewer deaths in the section, read like blessings filed as anomalies.

The twist sits in the recovered drive files. A doctor whose name is blacked out tried to turn the visits into interrogations about other SCPs, found his orders vanishing and his reports ignored, and wrote that he would confront SCP-343 the next day; after that he is simply gone: no records, no colleague who remembers him, and the inquiry is closed by an O5.

Meanwhile Dr. Beck asks to rotate staff through his section to lift morale in the rest of the Site, as if spreading the blessing around. The article never says outright that SCP-343 erased the doctor from existence, but every clue points there, and that unstated answer is what gives the cozy surface its edge.
